newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: New Slovenia takeover law vetoed in upper house.
newsitem.headline: New Slovenia takeover law vetoed in upper house.

text.p: Slovenia's State Council, the upper house of parliament, said on Tuesday it had vetoed the draft of a new takeover law in a bid to protect small shareholders.

According to the law, approved by the lower house of parliament last week, every transaction that exceeds 25 percent of a company's shares listed on the Ljubljana bourse would have to go through the government's Securities Market Agency.
The same would apply to any deal involving shares of companies with more than one billion tolars ($6.3 million) in equity capital or to smaller companies with more than 500 shareholders.

"The decision to veto the law followed an initiative by trade union representatives, who claim that the law would cause damage to small shareholders," State Council counsellor Emilijan Zlicar told Reuters.

Union representatives said that the draft left it unclear how small shareholders, who received their shares in the country's mass privatisation programme, would be able to manage their holdings, thus giving institutional investors an advantage.

The draft will now go back to the lower house, which is expected to repeat its vote as soon as possible. To be adopted, the law needs to be passed by an absolute majority of at least 46 out of 90 parliamentary votes. -- Novica Mihajlovic, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
